physical_ABI.receiver: Entry ECX is the actual stable aligned 12-byte {count,head,tail} root. The wrapper never changes ECX before its sole CALL.

physical_ABI.save_and_load: 004845A5 PUSH ESI; 004845A6 loads [ESP+8], exactly the original [entryESP+4]. ESI holds all32 payload bits across the scan and ordinary callee return.
physical_ABI.sole_CALL: 004845C2 PUSH EAX passes the exact first matching actual node; 004845C3 CALL 004837D0 retains the same actual root in ECX. No callback/provider shim is admissible.
physical_ABI.stack_derivation: For wrapper entry ESP=S: saved ESI is at S-4; matched node is pushed at S-8; erase entry ESP=S-12 and [eraseESP+4] is that found node. Accepted erase RET4 returns wrapper ESP to S-4; POP ESI restores S; wrapper RET4 leaves caller ESP=S+8.
physical_ABI.return: Every ordinary return yields full entry payload bits in EAX, including empty/absent and the post-free match arm. Both RET4 instructions start at 004845BF and 004845CB.
physical_ABI.ESI: Explicitly saved and restored; matched path depends on the accepted real erase/free ordinary ABI preserving nonvolatile ESI. No post-free node access occurs.
physical_ABI.other_registers: EBX/EDI/EBP are untouched locally and preserved through the ordinary callee ABI. On no-call paths ECX remains root and EDX remains incoming bits. Matched paths make no blanket volatile ECX/EDX, x87/SSE/MXCSR or DF preservation claim across CRT.
physical_ABI.flags: Empty/absent returns preserve the final TEST of zero: CF0/PF1/ZF1/SF0/OF0, AF undefined. Matched return preserves flags left by actual erase, whose saved readiness attributes final arithmetic flags to ADD ESP,4; count-decrement/CMP flags are not claimed to survive CRT.
physical_ABI.DF: No local DF/ES use or modification. A matched real erase/free call requires its ordinary current-CRT entry contract, including DF0; no blanket DF/FP claim across CRT.
physical_ABI.stale_saved_comment: Saved comment claims plain RET. Both independently verified physical sites are RET4. Worker records the discrepancy without mutation.

ordered_behavior: Load root.head from ECX+4 into EAX; TEST head; save ESI and load stacked borrowed payload without changing those flags.
Empty head branches directly to MOV EAX,ESI; POP ESI; RET4, making no erase call or root/node mutation.
Compare actual node.payload at node+8 against ESI; equality selects the first matching actual node in head-to-next order.
On inequality load actual node.next at node+4; TEST next and loop while nonzero. Exhaustion returns original payload through the early MOV/POP/RET4 arm.
For the first match push that exact EAX node and call the real accepted erase with ECX unchanged. Ignore its successor return, set EAX back to ESI, restore ESI and RET4. Stop after one match.

ordered_body: Load node.prev into EDX; save ESI. If previous exists, load node.next into ESI and write previous.next. Otherwise load node.next into EDX and write root.head.
Compare freshly read node.next against0, then freshly reload node.prev into EDX without changing flags.
If next exists, freshly load it into ESI, write next.prev=EDX, ADD root.count,-1, PUSH actual node and CALL free at004837FA.
If next is zero, ADD root.count,-1, PUSH actual node, XOR ESI,ESI, write root.tail=EDX, CALL free at00483811.
Each normal return executes ADD ESP,4; MOV EAX,ESI; POP ESI; RET4. Captured successor or0 survives free; no post-free node access or payload destructor.
saved_physical_ABI.stack: For entryESP=S, saved ESI isS-4, pushed node isS-8, free entryESP=S-12 and its actual pointer is[freeESP+4]. CDECL free returns toS-8; ADD4 restoresS-4, POP ESI restoresS, RET4 leaves callerESP=S+8.
saved_physical_ABI.return: EAX=actual successor captured in ESI before free, or0 on tail/singleton. ESI restored. No blanket ECX/EDX/x87/SSE/MXCSR/DF preservation across actual CRT; ordinary ABI preconditions apply.
saved_physical_ABI.flags: Final ADD ESP,4 determines arithmetic flags on normal return; MOV/POP/RET do not alter them. No inference that count-decrement flags survive free/epilogue.
saved_physical_ABI.native_DATA: No absolute native DATA cell, vtable, class allocator, singleton or hidden context is read by the79-byte body.
